description:
What this shows: Peer connectivity and overlay bandwidth for this node: peer counts, disconnects, total bytes and messages exchanged, and the transaction, proposal, and validation traffic that flows across the peer-to-peer network.
Use it to: Gauge peer health and overall overlay bandwidth and see which message types dominate network traffic.

panels.title: Active Peers
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Number of active inbound and outbound peer connections the node currently holds.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the inbound and outbound active-peer counts per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Outbound is what the node dials out; inbound is what others open to it. Both should be stable.*

###### Healthy range:
*roughly 10-21 outbound and 0-85 inbound on mainnet, depending on config.*

###### Watch for:
*Outbound dropping toward zero (isolation) or inbound pinned at the limit with churn (connection pressure).*

###### Source:
[PeerfinderManager.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/peerfinder/detail/PeerfinderManager.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logic Stats ctor`

panels.title: Peer Disconnects
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Peer connections that dropped, as a per-interval increase.*

###### How it's computed:
*Disconnect events per rate-interval, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A flat or slowly rising line is normal; the slope matters more than the absolute value.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; slow, steady growth.*

###### Watch for:
*Sharp step-ups in the slope (network instability, resource exhaustion, or many peers dropping the node at once).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.h)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl::Stats ctor`

panels.title: Total Network Bytes
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Total bytes received and sent across all peer connections.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second in/out byte rate per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Overall bandwidth footprint; in and out usually track network activity together.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*Sudden sustained jumps not matched by ledger or transaction activity (relay storms or a noisy peer).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: Total Network Messages
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Total messages received and sent across all peer connections.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second in/out message rate per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Overall message throughput of the overlay; complements the byte totals.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*Message count climbing far faster than bytes (many tiny messages, possible flooding).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: Transaction Traffic
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transaction relay messages in and out, plus duplicate transaction messages received.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second message rate for the transaction and transaction-duplicate categories.*

###### Reading it:
*In/out rise with network transaction volume; duplicates are transactions the node already had.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; duplicates a modest fraction of inbound.*

###### Watch for:
*Duplicate inbound approaching or exceeding unique inbound (redundant relay), or a sharp spike suggesting transaction flooding.*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: Proposal Traffic
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Consensus proposal messages in/out, plus untrusted and duplicate proposal messages received.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second message rate for the proposal, proposal-untrusted, and proposal-duplicate categories.*

###### Reading it:
*Trusted in/out track consensus rounds; untrusted come from validators not on this node's trusted list.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; untrusted and duplicates low relative to trusted.*

###### Watch for:
*High untrusted (trusted-list misconfiguration) or high duplicates (inefficient relay or proposal spam).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: Validation Traffic
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Validation messages in/out, plus untrusted and duplicate validation messages received.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second message rate for the validation, validation-untrusted, and validation-duplicate categories.*

###### Reading it:
*Trusted validations should arrive steadily each ledger; untrusted come from non-trusted validators.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; untrusted and duplicates low relative to trusted.*

###### Watch for:
*Rising untrusted or duplicate validations (trusted-list health issues or validation spam).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: Overlay Traffic by Category (Bytes In)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Top overlay traffic categories ranked by inbound bytes, excluding the all-traffic total.*

###### How it's computed:
*Top categories by inbound byte rate per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Shows which message types dominate receive bandwidth right now.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; transactions, proposals, and validations typically lead on a synced node.*

###### Watch for:
*A fetch or ledger-data category topping the list (sync activity) or an unexpected category dominating.*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: Duplicate Traffic (Wasted Bandwidth)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Throughput of duplicate transaction, proposal, and validation traffic: messages the node had already seen and discarded.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the duplicate byte counters for each category, in and out.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; this is bandwidth spent on redundant relays.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; a small fraction of total traffic.*

###### Watch for:
*Duplicate rate climbing toward the same order as useful traffic (poor relay topology or redundant flooding).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: All Traffic Categories (Detail)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The busiest overlay categories by inbound byte rate over time, excluding the all-traffic total.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second inbound byte rate for the busiest categories, ranked, excluding the all-traffic total.*

###### Reading it:
*Time-series companion to the category bar view; shows how the traffic mix shifts over the window.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A category ramping up and staying high, or the mix suddenly changing (sync, spam, or a misbehaving peer).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`
